coverage_contract.rule: Every manuscript built by paper/Makefile and every root manuscript PDF licensed by REUSE.toml must appear exactly once in artifacts. A rejected artifact must not be built, licensed, or present as a shipped manuscript.

artifacts.title: Tail Certificates and Achievement-Set Geometry for Erdős Problems 249 and 257
artifacts.claim_scope: Gateway exposition for Erdős Problems 249 and 257. For #249 it records the exact dyadic-section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1, infinite-dimensionality, the explicit finite Farey denominator exclusion, and diagonal certificates through t = 82, but no instance at t = 83 or unbounded family. For #257 it records checked restricted-support geometry and the remaining half-value and 1/21 branches. Both problems remain open, and the shared Lambert-series change of variables transfers no irrationality theorem.

artifacts.title: Problem-Sized Lean Worlds
artifacts.claim_scope: A first-principles architecture and access guide to the public Lean source, reviewed claim record, authored documents, generated views, release flow, CI jobs, and human trust boundary. It describes a working prototype rather than a validated multi-user service; as of 31 August 2026 no completed external cold-clone use or accepted external contribution had been recorded. A later historical example illustrates the limit of explicitly recorded checks; the guide adds no mathematical result.

artifacts.title: From a Cold Clone to a Proof Receipt
artifacts.claim_scope: An author-operated prototype case study of zero-build corpus navigation, explicit authority boundaries, replayable agent-session receipts, focused changed-cone builds, and exact cached dependency-index validation in this repository. As of 31 August 2026 no external contributor had completed the tour or documented return path. It does not claim autonomous proving, optimal reasoning, external mathematical novelty, demonstrated outside usability, or transfer to another project.

artifacts.title: From Spare Compute to Cumulative Mathematics
artifacts.claim_scope: A strategy and working-prototype paper for an open research commons that accepts compute, mathematical direction, architecture improvements, cold-clone cleanup, and review. It defines role-bounded contribution packets, a candidate-to-attention funnel, provenance-preserving adoption, and evaluation measures. As of 31 August 2026 no completed external cold clone or accepted external contribution had been recorded. All eight Erdős problems remain open; the paper reports no measured discovery-rate improvement, independent mathematical review, proof of optimal architecture, or community acceptance of a new mathematical result.

artifacts.title: The Binary Totient Series
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 249. It distinguishes checked premises and finite certificates from open obligations: the level-e dyadic-section rank is 2^e+1 only for e >= 1; the full span is infinite-dimensional; the finite Farey computation excludes denominators up to the stated bound; and diagonal certificates exist through t = 82, with neither t = 83 nor an unbounded family supplied. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 257. It separates checked finite-support and restricted-achievement-set structure from the missing Booleanisation and tail steps. No finite rank-at-least-two support represents 1/21; the primitive 2p+3q cone has the stated coverage and recurrent multiplicities, but the eventual affine-supercapacity regime survives. The universal, half-value, and 1/21 membership questions remain open.

artifacts.title: A Basis for the 2-Kernel of Euler's Totient
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 249, ordered unconditional results first: the exact level-e dyadic totient section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1 and the resulting infinite-dimensionality; the explicit finite-Farey denominator exclusion; the phi*mu Lambert weight separating #249 from the settled omega/Omega/tau series; the exact supplier-fibre bijection together with its global-isolation counterexample; and scoped method no-go theorems. Lean checks diagonal certificates for every t <= 82, but supplies neither t = 83 nor the unbounded family equivalent to irrationality. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Denominator Periods, Rational-Value Constraints and Achievement-Set Geometry
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 257 led by exact finite-period noncollapse, necessary structure for any rational-valued infinite support, and achievement-set geometry. Duverney–Tachiya settle squarefree support for every power-of-two base, including base 2; this does not cover arbitrary bases b >= 3. The manuscript separately proves that two divisibility-first certificate engines miss this settled value and that irrationality is invariant under finite support changes via checked prefix/tail lemmas. No finite rank-at-least-two support sums to 1/21, while the quotient-greedy classification leaves an eventual affine-supercapacity regime unexcluded. Tao–Teräväinen prove prime support at base 2. Universal Erdős #257, the half-value test, and 1/21 membership remain open.

artifacts.title: Factorial-Channel Obstructions and Exact Orbit Boundaries
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos68 modules. Lean checks the exact factorial-successor and eventual-unit-carry frontiers, integral-channel and prime-translator identities, weighted projection consumers, zero-plateau and prime-power branch reductions, and the Cramer residual identity. An independently regenerated exact GMP certificate supplies one non-unit carry at m = 300000, and a Lean theorem consumes that finite fact to exclude every smaller positive rational denominator. No theorem supplies cofinally many non-unit carries, the weighted collision and complementary-residue estimates, cofinal lower-cylinder escape, doubled-prime branch failure, or Cramer residual nonintegrality; Erdős Problem 68 remains open.

artifacts.title: Excluding the Bounded Negative Part
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos243 modules. Lean checks constant- and scoped periodic-negative exclusions, eventual vanishing from an eventually bounded negative part plus normalised vanishing, and exclusion of finite normalised negative mass. Eventual strict centring is not an independent hypothesis because normalised vanishing supplies it after a finite shift. Koizumi supplies normalised vanishing for the canonical orbit; boundedness of its negative part is not supplied. Mixed-sign classification and the unbounded divergent-mass branch remain open, so Erdős Problem 243 remains open.

artifacts.title: An Integral-Shift Criterion for Dyadic Tail Recurrences
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos251 module. Lean checks the infinite prime/gap equivalence conditional on summability, denominator collapse for rational dyadic recurrences, unboundedness and non-eventual-periodicity of the actual prime gaps, and the exact local implication from cofinally recurring adjacent small-mismatch tail shifts to failure of eventual integrality. The prime-number-theorem summability and concrete prime-gap-tail instantiation are paper proofs; no theorem supplies the required cofinal adjacent small-mismatch pairs, and Erdős Problem 251 remains open.

artifacts.title: The Three-Prime Running Least Common Multiple
artifacts.claim_scope: The paper proves, using Bugeaud–Laurent's external Hecke–Mahler theorem, that for every pair of distinct primes both the de-duplicated and repeated-running-LCM sums are transcendental; these analytic deductions are not Lean-formalised. For three primes, Lean checks exact logarithmic-cell and finite height-fibre structure, the dyadic block alphabet {2,6,10,30}, residue arithmetic, and the conditional absorption-and-cancellation core. The scan over 106,666 denominator/start pairs is bounded evidence only. Rationality-to-carry identification, the required divisibility, and a cofinal escape producer are unproved; Problem 269 remains open from three primes onward.

artifacts.title: Critical-Value Separation and Admissible Hubs
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of ErdosProblems.Erdos1041. The paper proves an all-degree critical-value-separation regime by a resolved inverse branch, the area formula, Polya's area-capacity inequality, and an exact coefficient estimate; a sharp all-degree collinear theorem; a complete primitive sparse quintic theorem; and translated cubic and quartic quotient-fibre theorems in degrees 3q and 4q for q >= 2; and the sharp critical-value budget sum_j |f(c_j)|^(1/n) <= (n-1)R for every enclosing disk in degrees two through five. Those separation and solved-family assemblies are ordinary mathematics, not kernel-checked authority. Lean checks Newton-flow value decay, the exponential first integral, the oriented-ray connection obstruction, the exact common-translation collision locus, finite affine-line avoidance, root retention under small constant perturbations, and the three solved-family kernels selected by ExternalVerification1041SolvedFamilies. The note identifies an invalid three-ended local saddle block in the printed proof of Proposition 12 of a March 2026 manuscript; it does not refute the proposition, and a four-pronged or cut-annulus repair may exist. Near-tied critical values and multiple saddles are excluded; the global decomposition, perturbation stability, and strict length gluing are not proved; Erdos Problem 1041 remains open.

artifacts.title: Sharp Height and Four-Jet Obstructions at Base $3/2$
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of scoped no-go and counting results for Erdős Problem 1049, not an irrationality theorem. Lean checks scalar-content neutrality, the endpoint exclusion of 2 and 3 under unit hypotheses, four-jet cancellation at the stated rank threshold, a coordinatewise-clearing corridor obstruction and tail recurrence at 3/2, and the elementary height inequality needed by Bundschuh–Väänänen's external criterion at 7/2. The external analytic argument is not formalised. Polynomial-factor, cross-row, primitive-family, nonzero-pair, and analytic-remainder routes remain untreated; the rational-base problem remains open.

artifacts.title: The Factorial-Denominator Series: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 68. It assembles exact factorial-successor, carry, channel, projection, and finite denominator results while keeping every conditional hypothesis and failed route visible. The finite certificate excludes rational denominators below the stated bound but supplies no cofinal divisibility-miss producer. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Reciprocal-Tail Rigidity: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 243. It assembles the centred-state identity, negative-mass recovery, bounded-rise and periodic no-go results, and the conditional bounded-negative exclusion while retaining the full state, residue, and mechanism context. Mixed-sign unbounded negative excursions remain uncontrolled, so the original eventual-recurrence problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Prime Gaps and Dyadic Tails: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 251. It assembles exact prime-gap summation identities, rationality-to-integral-shift reductions, cofinal small-mismatch consumers, and countermodels that delimit the method. No theorem supplies the required cofinal mismatch for the actual prime-gap series, so irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: The Three-Prime Running LCM: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 269. It assembles the two-prime benchmark, literal three-prime block digits, shell recurrences, residue and carry forms, finite contradictions, and observer limitations. In the registered release slice the actual rationality-to-reduced-carry bridge and the cofinal window-escape producer remain open, so the three-prime irrationality endpoint is not claimed.

artifacts.title: Lemniscates and Newton Flow: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 1041. It assembles Newton-flow decay, critical-value ray separation, translation-collision geometry, root retention, solved structured families, and the diagnosed gap in the claimed global saddle argument. The general spanning-tree and metric-gluing endpoint remains open.

artifacts.title: Rational-Base Lambert Series: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 1049. It assembles rational-base tail recurrences and forcing bounds, the base-three-halves coordinatewise no-go theorem, height-region specialisations, and Hermite–Padé and Mahler-system frontiers. These results do not prove irrationality at base three halves or the universal rational-base assertion, both of which remain open.
